title: Hotel Booking
summary: Search hotels, hold rooms during checkout and reserve per-night inventory in one transaction so the last room is never double-booked.
narrative:
Guests search hotels by city and dates, see room types with prices and availability, reserve, pay and cancel. This question is more about product design than raw scale: list the features first, then design the database and APIs around them. Using ByteByteGo's sizing, 5,000 hotels with 1 M rooms at ~70 % occupancy and ~3-night stays give ~240 K reservations/day ≈ 3 reservations/s, with searches ~100× that (≈ 300/s). The API: GET /hotels?city&checkIn&checkOut, GET /hotels/{id}/rooms?checkIn&checkOut, POST /reservations (creates a HOLD), POST /reservations/{id}/payment and DELETE /reservations/{id}.

Use a relational SQL database: ACID transactions and constraints matter more than raw scale here, and one inventory row per room type per night (≈ 5,000 hotels × ~20 room types × 2 years ≈ 73 M rows) fits comfortably. Tables: hotel, room_type, room_type_inventory(hotel_id, room_type_id, date, total, reserved) and reservation(id, guest_id, hotel_id, room_type_id, check_in, check_out, status HOLD|CONFIRMED|CANCELLED|EXPIRED, hold_expires_at, idempotency_key). A room type is available for a stay when every night in [check_in, check_out) has total - reserved ≥ the rooms requested. Reserving a room is one transaction that, for each night, runs UPDATE … SET reserved = reserved + 1 WHERE … AND reserved < total and rolls back if any night updates no row (optimistic locking with a version column works too), so two simultaneous bookings of the last room can't both succeed. POST /reservations takes an idempotency key, unique on the reservation row, so a retried click returns the existing reservation instead of booking twice.

While a guest is checking out, the reservation is a HOLD that already counts in reserved and expires after ~10 min, so nobody else can take that room. The Web Server initiates payment with the Payment Service against the reservation, using the reservation id as the payment's idempotency key, and payment success moves HOLD → CONFIRMED. A Task Scheduler triggers an expiry job on a Worker that moves unpaid holds past hold_expires_at to EXPIRED and releases their nights in the same transaction. Confirmation and expiry both update the reservation only WHERE status = 'HOLD', so exactly one of them wins; a payment that loses to expiry is refunded. Cancellation also releases the nights. Hotel search runs on a Search Index and hotel details and rates are cached, but availability is always checked against the database. Optionally the Worker sends confirmation and hold-expiry emails through the Notification Service, and Monitoring tracks failed reservations and expiring holds.

functional: Search hotels by city and dates through the Search Index; serve hotel details and rates from Cache
Check availability in SQL: every night of the stay needs total - reserved ≥ the rooms requested
Reserve in one transaction of conditional per-night updates with an idempotency key, creating a ~10 min HOLD
Pay against the reservation through the Payment Service and confirm the HOLD; cancel to release the nights
Run a scheduled expiry job on Workers that marks unpaid holds EXPIRED and releases their nights
nonFunctional: 5,000 hotels and 1 M rooms; ~240 K reservations/day ≈ 3/s; searches ~100× ≈ 300/s
Never double-book the last room under concurrent reservations or retried clicks
Keep search and hotel details fast without serving stale availability
constraints: Clients must never query the SQL Database directly; all reads and writes go through the booking API
Payments are initiated by the backend against a reservation; Client-to-Payment Service paths pass through Web Servers
Check availability and reserve against SQL, never from the Search Index or Cache
Make payment confirmation and hold expiry conditional on status HOLD so only one of them wins
capacity: ≈ 73 M inventory rows (5,000 hotels × ~20 room types × 2 years); holds expire after ~10 min
specs.tradeoff: Conditional updates inside one relational transaction rule out double-booking, and at a few reservations per second contention is low; optimistic version checks avoid locks but force retries on popular dates. Holds protect a guest during checkout but keep rooms off the market for ~10 min when checkout is abandoned, and a payment that loses to expiry must be refunded.
specs.bonus: Connect Worker → Notification Service for confirmation and hold-expiry emails, and add Monitoring for failed reservations and expiring holds.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two Web Servers so search and booking survive one instance failure.
Connect the Task Scheduler to a Worker that releases expired holds.

hints: Start with Client → Load Balancer → Web Server. Connect Web Server → Search Index for hotel search, → Cache for hotel details and rates, and → SQL Database for inventory and reservations.

Reserve with one transaction of conditional per-night updates (reserved < total) plus an idempotency key, creating a ~10 min HOLD. Connect Web Server → Payment Service to pay against it, and Web Server → Task Scheduler → Worker → SQL Database to release expired holds.

Run two Web Servers; each reaches the Search Index, SQL, Cache, Payment Service, Task Scheduler and Monitoring. Wire Task Scheduler → Worker → SQL Database, and Worker → Notification Service for confirmation emails.
